description.narrative: PARC, in partnership with Oxfam, will carry out a quick assessment and consultation to identify the best tool/app that would be developed to support farmers in areas of good agricultural practices, seasonal calendar, weather forecasts etc., depending on the needsand on pre-existing applications or tools developed, PARC will work with a consultant to identify and design such tool. The app aims to serve more than 7000 smallholder farmers, the application will offer a wide range of services that serves theagricultural sector (farmers and herders). Among the benefits that the app offers are the weather forecast, suggestions related to farming, pesticides, and the best crops to grow each season. It also shows the seasonal calendar. Digital transformation and expansion of all digital services have become a global orientation and approach adopted by various countries of the world, as well as the fact that attention to knowledge issues in technology and digitization must be imposed by the economic and social development challenges of Palestine's agricultural sector, with growing calls for the need to keep pace with the requirements of the so-called fourth industrial revolution and the opportunities and challenges it poses. An electronic agricultural platform has been established to help support the agricultural sector and build productive infrastructure for the agricultural sector and agricultural development. Agricultural digital transformation is an evolutionary process based on modern technology to digitize work in the agricultural sector. It connects all partsof the agricultural system, including holders, peasants, enterprises working in the agricultural sector, agricultural companies, technicians, agricultural engineers and the Ministry of Agriculture,with the aim of showing and marketing all agricultural products grown in the country, agricultural production supplies, agricultural auxiliary services and cooperative societies through digitizationof research, studies, references and agricultural experiments to benefit small farmers and professionals.

participating-org.narrative: In 1983 a small group of agronomists founded the Palestinian Agricultural Relief Committees (PARC), which has since developed into one of the most important Palestinian non-governmental organisations providing services to poor and marginalised farmers onthe West Bank and Gaza Strip, working to make agricultural businesses grow. PARC#s goal is to promote an economic and social climate that would allow the Palestinian agricultural sector to develop sustainably. Another goal is to improve the living standard of Palestinians living in rural areas, especially of poor farming families. PARC provides a broad range of agricultural extension services. It is active in land reclamation and in building rural access roads. The organisation advocates the improvementof rural women#s economic position. It is part of an Oxfam Novib-funded three-year gender-focus program. In 1991 PARC got an ISO-certification. It was the first and so far only non-governmental organisation in the Arab world to obtain one. It has also developed an impressive strategic ten-year plan for the 1998-2008 period. Together with several other agricultural non-governmental organisations (NGOs) PARC has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Agriculture, which sees PARC#s workasindependent and complementary to its own. PARC is active in a network of Palestinian NGOs and a member of the governing committee of the Palestinian NGO-network. Oxfam Novib has been supporting PARC since 1982. In 1999 Oxfam Novib, ICCO, Christian Aid (UK) and Oxfam Great Britain set up a donor consortium to support PARC. This provides PARC a measure of long-term financial security. It also makes technical and organisational assistance available to PARC in further developing its program.
